assessment.executive_summary: The repository implements a compact customer onboarding service. It accepts onboarding requests, validates customer data, prevents duplicate e-mail addresses, calls an external KYC provider, calculates a risk score, activates low-risk customers or routes risky cases to manual review, persists the customer and publishes an onboarding event.
assessment.system_purpose: Start and track customer onboarding with KYC-based risk assessment and customer status management.

functional_view.summary: The system starts customer onboarding, checks for duplicate e-mail addresses, performs KYC, calculates risk, assigns ACTIVE or MANUAL_REVIEW status, persists the customer and exposes status lookup.

user_or_system_flows.name: Start onboarding
user_or_system_flows.description: A client posts an onboarding request; the service rejects duplicates, calls KYC, scores risk, stores the customer and publishes an event.

user_or_system_flows.name: Read onboarding status
user_or_system_flows.description: A client reads the persisted customer status and review reason by customer id.

technical_view.summary: The implementation is a Spring-style service with REST controllers, an application service, repository persistence, an outbound KYC HTTP call, Kafka event publishing, OpenAPI contracts and SOAP/WSDL examples.

decision_basis.decision_summary: The repository is suitable as a compact decision-grade demonstration of codebase understanding, but not production-ready without configuration, testing, CI and observability hardening.

recommended_actions.title: Externalize the risk threshold
recommended_actions.rationale: The code hard-codes riskScore > 70 while application.yml also contains risk.threshold.

recommended_actions.title: Implement executable scenario tests
recommended_actions.rationale: The test class names important scenarios but the methods are placeholders.

tradeoffs.topic: Keep modular service vs split services
options: Keep the compact modular service and extract policies/configuration first
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep the modular service for this codebase size; extract decision policy and integration configuration before considering service splits.

readiness.rationale: Business flow and contracts are understandable, but tests, CI, observability and configuration usage are incomplete.

tool_positioning.summary: For this repository, the pack produces a structured source-evidence report that combines functional reverse engineering, interface extraction, process/readiness findings and refactoring recommendations; this positions it as an LLM-first complement or alternative to traditional code inventory and documentation tools.
strengths_vs_traditional_tools: Connects business behavior, contracts, flows and refactoring recommendations in one evidence-backed report
Uses Codex/LLM semantic extraction instead of treating code-map navigation hints as final facts
Produces portfolio-ready HTML and JSON artifacts
boundaries: The CLI prepares context and validates evidence, but Codex/LLM performs semantic extraction
Visible security risks can be extracted from source evidence, but specialized SAST remains complementary
Claims are limited to files present in the repository

top_risks.title: Risk threshold is duplicated
top_risks.description: The service uses a hard-coded threshold of 70 while configuration also defines risk.threshold.

top_risks.title: Tests are only placeholders
top_risks.description: The test class names relevant scenarios but does not contain assertions in this demo repository.

recommended_next_steps.title: Move risk threshold into configuration
recommended_next_steps.reason: This prevents divergence between configuration and implementation.

recommended_next_steps.title: Turn scenario tests into executable assertions
recommended_next_steps.reason: The repository already names important test scenarios but the methods are empty.

open_questions: The repository does not show authentication or authorization requirements for the onboarding endpoints.
